The time the process started after system boot.
The PID of the parent of this process.
the value is expressed in clock ticks (divide by sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)).
This file contains the initial environment that was set when the currently executing program was started via execve(2).
this file will not reflect those changes.
If, after an execve(2), the process modifies its argv strings, those changes will show up here.
If the process is well-behaved, it is a set of strings separated by null bytes ('\0'), with a further null byte after the last string.
Think of this file as the command line that the process wants you to see.
since Linux 5.9, the reading process must have either CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE in the initial (i.e., root) user namespace.
